video_title: What If The Jaylen Brown Trade Isn't Actually Bad?

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Boston's willingness to pay top-tier players versus Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: Clearly there's a line. They're willing to pay a top-10 level player that much money.
quotes.quote: I think for Boston, obviously they were clearly willing to pay two guys 60-plus million dollars since they pursued Giannis Antetokounmpo, but there's a line. Clearly there's a line. They're willing to pay a top-10 level player that much money. Jason Tatum they perceive as that, Giannis Antetokounmpo is undoubtedly that, but Jaylen Brown, clearly Boston does not perceive as being that level of player.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Boston's original plan to sell high on Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: Boston went into the 2025-26 season planning on selling high on Jaylen Brown if an offer made sense.
quotes.quote: I heard this in the middle of the season that Boston went into the 2025-26 season planning on selling high on Jaylen Brown if an offer was out there that made sense. But plans changed. They were on a 50-plus win pace, Jason Tatum was healthy enough to come back, and they're like, you know what, we'll just stick with it and keep rolling this year and see what happens in the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the efficiency trade-off between Paul George and Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: They're going from a higher volume average efficiency Jaylen Brown to a lower volume higher efficiency Paul George.
quotes.quote: You can look at the Paul George side of it. Paul George is a 40% guy on catch-and-shoot threes, Jaylen Brown 35%, a better spot-up shooter. You can look at last year, 25 games with Philadelphia, Paul George was the more efficient pick-and-roll scorer. He was the more efficient isolation scorer. Jaylen Brown was far less efficient in those play types. So they're going from a higher volume average efficiency Jaylen Brown to a lower volume higher efficiency Paul George.

quotes.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White's superior season and Team USA snub
quotes.excerpt: The Celtics did not feel like Jaylen had the best season on their team... they felt that Derrick White had a better season.

text_blocks.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
text_blocks.text: Derrick White is catching a lot of flak here from Brian Windhorst's comments last night in the emergency pod that he did, that Brian Windhorst is connecting the dots here saying the Celtics did not feel like Jaylen had the best season on their team. They felt that Derrick White had a better season. I also think you can look at Team USA. In 2024, after he won a Finals MVP, who was left off the Team USA roster and who was put onto it? It was Derrick White, not Jaylen Brown.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
text_blocks.texts: And he felt a certain way about that.

quotes.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
quotes.summary_phrase: Boston's preference for on-ball defense and high-energy play
quotes.excerpt: They wanted a better on-ball defender, a guy that would be playing high-energy defense.
quotes.quote: Grant Hill went on the record to explain that they wanted a better on-ball defender, a guy that would be playing high-energy defense, and Derrick White and Jrue Holiday made more sense on that front filling a roster spot with those two guys rather than Jaylen Brown. And so you can look at this and say the Boston Celtics feel like they have a redundancy in Jaylen Brown's skill set, which is he's a high-volume, high-isolation guy, dribble-drive guy, not a great three-point shooter.

quotes.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
quotes.summary_phrase: Payton Pritchard's potential as a bucket-getter
quotes.excerpt: People laugh at the notion that he could be a mini Jaylen Brunson.
quotes.quote: And then there's Payton Pritchard. I know people laugh at the notion that he could be a mini Jaylen Brunson. I'm not saying he's going to be a Finals MVP and an All-NBA player. I'm not suggesting that. What I'm saying is when you look at the numbers and when you watch him, the guy is a bucket-getter. And we saw Jaylen Brunson go from a Dallas Mavericks team as a backup, could not get the right oxygen and minutes to prove that he is an All-Star caliber player until he left to go to the New York.

quotes.speaker: Tom Haberstroh
quotes.summary_phrase: Payton Pritchard's statistical production in Jaylen Brown's absence
quotes.excerpt: In the games in which Jaylen Brown did not play, Payton Pritchard was an all-league level player.
quotes.quote: In the games in which Jaylen Brown did not play, Payton Pritchard was an all-league level player, averaging 25 points a game, seven assists, and five rebounds in those 10 games last year. And he was a Sixth Man of the Year two years ago. The numbers don't lie when it comes to Payton Pritchard's potential to breakout next season.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Data Baller's analysis of Payton Pritchard's efficiency
quotes.excerpt: Without Jaylen Brown last season, Payton Pritchard averaged 27 points, 7.6 assists, five boards on 61% true shooting.
quotes.quote: One of the screenshots you had on your story was a graphic from Data Baller looking at Payton Pritchard's numbers per 75 possessions versus with Jaylen Brown on the floor versus without Jaylen Brown on the floor. And without Jaylen Brown last season, Payton Pritchard averaged 27 points, 7.6 assists, five boards on 61% true shooting. I know one of the best Celtics reporters out there, Noah Dalzell, she gets ragged on sometimes a few years ago for saying Payton Pritchard will be an All-Star someday. If it's going to happen, it's going to be this year.
